key_insight: The paper proposes Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI), a new inverse-problem paradigm that solves problems by exploiting mathematical or physical structure instead of iterative objective minimization.
engineering_relevance: SDI could improve efficiency, interpretability, and parameter decoupling in inverse problems relevant to PDE-based modeling, imaging, and scientific machine learning.
method: MSDI: build a pseudo-inverse in the spectral domain using unitary diagonalization.
PSDI: recover solutions via physical structure, including virtual-source projection for waveform inversion imaging.
PSDBP: use three structural projections to guide deep neural networks through a physical-system analogy.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and paradigm-setting; it does not report experimental datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: The approach is presented at a framework level, so practical gains will depend on whether the required mathematical or physical structure is available and stable in real problems.
paper_title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm for Solving Inverse Problems
